utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. I was advised that Mr. Karadzic has something to raise before we hear the evidence today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to do that in a private session. I will only need a couple of minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor or Mr. Tieger, can I get a confirmation from the Prosecution that, in relation to these 16 sniping incidents, no expert is coming as a Prosecution witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct. There will be fact witnesses about other sniping incidents, but this the only expert specifically about sniping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber wasn't aware of the fact that this witness is the only witness who will testify as to the origin of these 16 sniping incidents as an expert. On that basis, we allow you, Mr. Karadzic, to go until the end of today, given that you said you would need two or three sessions more, upon the condition that the Chamber will exercise a robust control over the efficient and relevant conduct of your cross-examination. We'll bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're extremely grateful to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, allow me to excuse myself, because I was actually coming in because of the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Depending on the situation, we may need you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, but you may be excused now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden, I apologise for the inconvenience. There were some matters to deal with in your absence, so it has transpired that you need to stay with us a bit longer than expected; probably until the end of today. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry. Before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry. Before we go on, Mr. President, we do have, I estimate, 45 minutes of redirect, and some additional time, depending on today's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Bear that in mind, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we can comply with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before we move on to incident number 4, from Schedule F, I would like to thank you once again for the calculation of the angles that you did in your spare time. I would also like to tell you that we are still looking for information relating to the detour of the tram. The Defence will act in a fair manner and will take all of the options into consideration. That is to say, we need to establish at which point in time this S-curve on the tracks was moved further down towards Holiday Inn. Can you tell us, in short and based on your notes, what does Incident 4 from the Schedule F refer to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Case F4 is the incident when a 35-year-old woman and her 8-year-old daughter were shot by a single bullet while walking together on Ivana Krndelja Street in central Sarajevo. The bullet wounded the mother in her left thigh and the daughter in her right hand and her abdomen, her stomach. The alleged shooting position was Ozrenska Street, and the GPS coordinate is as the one above in the paper document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the then Ivana Krndelja Street is now called Aziza Sacirbegovic Street? Are you aware of that, although I believe that you will trust my word for that, but in order to avoid any confusion in the future, can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know. I only visit that location according to the GPS coordinate and as shown to me by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the Court please produce 1D02159, page 2. First, let's look at page 1 to identify the document, and then page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We were informed that that was a zone of sniping activity. Was that zone there before the incident and after the incident? Have you received the interpretation of my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not -- nothing on my left screen. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you not bring in the English? It's not appearing on my computer either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before that, I would kindly ask you to tell us this: Were you informed that that place was a customary place of sniper activity? Was there sniper activity before the incident and was there any after the incident? Could you please answer that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to read that back in the witness statements, but I cannot recall it out of my head. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 6. I can see only the Serbian version, but I believe that you will find it in English as well. The Serbian text starts with the following words: "I never saw or heard ..." Could you please consult the paragraph in question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that there's no English translation at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, I'm going to read for the witness and for the other participants in the trial. I'm reading from paragraph 6: "I never heard or saw that anybody was hit in that street. We were the first and the last who were hit from a sniper weapon in that weapon [as interpreted]. I know that because my husband is a military commander and he is abreast of all the details. Later on, I learned, when we were already in hospital, that within that one hour a total of five people were hit from a sniper in that area, but not in that same street, and those people have been taken to the same hospital ..." And so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this jog your memory? Or, rather, did you have this witness statement at your disposal when you drew your conclusions about this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I no longer have access to this -- to this -- the witness statements of this incident, since I had them for the previous report, but I no longer have access. I do, however, recall the mentioning -- at the incident site, the mentioning of a screen for protection of civilians which would be in place only if there was a need for it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender Nafa Taric's statement, if it hasn't been admitted yet, as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you are well aware of the practice by this Tribunal. The witness did not confirm anything about this document, and there's no foundation on our part to admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, the witness did have that witness statement available to him. That is the only witness statement, and the witness had it when he drafted the expert report. He had the statement available to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I missed that point because we didn't have the English translation of this document. Mr. Gaynor, do you agree that this is the statement this witness had seen at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, he -- according to page 79 of Mr. van der Weijden's report, at the foot of the page, we see that he had the witness statement of this person, dated 12th November 1995 and 25th September of 2001, two separate statements, so they did form part of the material provided to Mr. van der Weijden. I leave it to Your Honours' discretion as to what to do with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why do we not have that English translation? Because they couldn't locate --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I've just been provided by Mr. Reid the 65 ter number for that. It's 09940 [Realtime transcript read in error "05490"]. And the 65 ter number for the statement of the 25th of September, 2001, is 10061.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The 65 ter number of the document which we see now is -- could you give it again? 5490?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The numbers I read out for the 1995 and 2001 statement, it's the same 65 ter number applies to the English and to the B/C/S, Mr. Reid tells me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D664, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, this is an expert witness, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. Just to correct the record, it's been pointed out to me that the number on the transcript is -- has been taken down wrong. The first 65 ter number is 09940. The other 65 ter number is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I would like to say that this is an expert witness and not an eye-witness. Even if he hadn't seen the incident, he should have seen it. An expert -- or, rather, things should be admitted if the expert should have seen them, and he did see them. He did see this thing during the drafting of the expert report. 1D02160 is the next document that I would like to call up. It's a photo that was signed by Mrs. Nafa Taric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden, are you familiar with this photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen this photo before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the photo depicts?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photo depicts a view from the incident site to the south, and the black squares depict the three containers that were placed there to hide the civilians from view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where the mother and the daughter were hit, in which parts of the body?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were hit as described in the situation -- the mother was hit in her left thigh and the daughter was wounded in her right hand and in her stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were those gun-shot wounds -- entry/exit wounds, rather, and were they both shot with a single bullet?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information provided to me, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They were standing up, or, rather, they were walking when they were hit; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the position of a victim important when it comes to determining the bullet trajectory, or, rather, is it important whether the victims were moving and where the site of the bullet entry is?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the positions of the two persons at the moment when they were shot, in this photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll mark with red [marks]. They were about in this location, according to my information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any containers or any other obstacles there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time of my visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the witness statement and the information provided to me, there were. There were three containers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In which direction were the two persons moving at the moment when the incident happened, when they were shot at?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were moving from east to west, in the direction of this arrow [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We still didn't hear from you whether they were shot at by a single bullet -- or, rather, you did say that it was a single bullet, did you not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, according to my information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they both suffer entry/exit wounds, or, in other words, did the bullet exit from both the victims' bodies?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it was a single bullet and the wounds were as described in the situation, they would both have entry/exit wounds -- entry/exit wounds, but the daughter might have an extra entry wound in her stomach as well, but I wouldn't know because it doesn't state here that. The mother, at least, because she was, according to my information, walking along, I think, the left side, but I would have to read the witness statement again for that. But they would both have entry and exit wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In a nutshell, the bullet was never found and it was never shown to you; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if the bullet was never found, but it was never shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that why you had to conclude in your report about the calibre based on the wound and the distance, because you were not given any information about the calibre; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Sarajevo police or the Muslim police conclude the calibre -- what was the calibre in question? At the moment of the investigation, they could do that; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to read the witness statements for that. But if they -- if there was a bullet, they should be able to conclude what calibre it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that they could have done that based on the entry wound? They could have concluded, based on the entry wound, what the calibre was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because they would need the bullet, itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did they tell you about the levels of the entry and exit wounds? Were the two points at the same level?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not -- I cannot remember being given that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But that information would be crucial for you to determine the direction and the point from which the shot was fired; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would help, but it would not be crucial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, if the entry and exit wounds were at the same distance from the ground, then we could conclude that the bullet was shot from the same level and from this very street; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily so. The entry doesn't have to be exactly in the same line as the exit wound. It depends on what tissue is in the way of the bullet and if any bone structure is hit or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the bullet in question hit a single bone in any of the two victims?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the horizon of this hilltop -- or, rather, the top of the hill is some 50 metres from the foot of the hill?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be, more or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For example, if the bullet had been fired from the foot, then the wounds would be parallel with the ground. If, however, the bullet was fired from the top, it would have hit the bodies at a certain angle. Right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would always be an angle, since a bullet is not a laser. It follows a parabolic, even at ground level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the parabola would be wider if the bullet had been fired from the hilltop?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The angle would be greater, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 74 of your report, you excluded 7.62-calibre with 39-millimetre charge because the distance would have been extreme, at the very far end of the range. And you have also excluded calibres bigger than 7.92 because the tissue damage would have been far greater. Right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I'm sorry, I have to correct. I did not exclude it, but it would be very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You didn't exclude 7.62 and 39 millimetres; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've written it would be at the extreme range and would be very inaccurate, and therefore, in my opinion, there would be three calibres that would be more likely used than this one. So I did not exclude it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Its velocity at the end, while passing through the two human bodies, would be much lower if the former one was in question; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the 7.62 times 39 had been used, the exit speed after passing through two bodies would be lower than with the other bullets, depending, of course, on the range fired, because if the other bullets had been fired from a greater range, the speed might be the same as the 7.62 times 39 millimetres that would be fired from a shorter range.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to your conclusions, where was the bullet fired from, eventually?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bullet, according to my conclusions, was fired from -- we have to switch to page 75 of the paper version. Could I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We can call it up, but perhaps you can mark the assumed place from which the bullet was fired in the photo. Then I would like to tender the photo into evidence and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be an indication, but I could -- I can do that [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That would have been the range; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Somewhere from this -- within this area, the shot would have originated, to my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Two hundred metre --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two hundred metres would be the end of the street at the T-junction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that's the distance from the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you put the date and signature on this picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit -- just a second. What's the number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D665.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before we remove the photo, did I understand you properly? Was that supposed to be between 200 and 1.104 metres? That's the area from which the shot came; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been. Only the houses higher up the hill have better views than the houses on street level, because the houses on street level would have absolutely no insight -- would only view the victims at a very late time after clearing the containers. So more likely they would be higher up the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But then it also proves that the distance was a bit bigger?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you -- could you clarify that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If, from the foot of the hill, from the 200 metres, towards the top, the visibility is what it is, and the higher you climb, the distance ranges from 200 metres to 1.104; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the Court please produce the same photo from page 75, 14045. This is from the gentleman's report, page 75 of his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does the name "Ozrenska Street" ring any bells, Mr. van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was named as the shooting position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your photo, is Ozrenska marked in red?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the top photo of page 75, Ozrenska is the red line within the field of fire just before 1104 metres, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to take a blue pen and draw another blue line parallel with Ozrenska Street, just to avoid any ambiguity in locating Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is just to the north of the red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Kindly put today's date and initial the photo. I would like to tender it and move on.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender just this page, because the document has probably already been admitted as a whole. We need the picture to stay on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden, were you ever informed that the separation line went along Ozrenska Street throughout the entire duration of the war; that the Serbs were on one side and that the Muslims were on the other side of Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only made aware of that Serb forces were on Ozrenska Street, but I wasn't informed that it was the exact location -- separation line where the Bosnian forces also were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you informed about any other separation lines?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me. I was told that we have technical difficulties today and it's not possible for us to keep any marked pictures for this moment. Another option we can think of is to use a video shot later on. But as far as this picture is concerned, if you look at the e-court version, Ozrenska Street is already marked, so we don't have to keep this, necessarily. So we can move on at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At this distance from Ozrenska Street to the place of the incident, were there any troops there? And if there were, which troops were those? And my previous question was this: Have you been informed about any other separation lines, save for this one along the Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we again see the witness's statement, please. The ERN is 0105-6125 - 1D - P664. We had it on the screen a minute ago, and it was admitted a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to page 2, please. We have already read the sixth paragraph, and we heard that there were no sniper incidents either before or after. And the witness only suggests that the shot might have come from Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that from a distance of 1.000 metres or, rather, 1.104 metres, this victim that provided a statement as a witness indicated Ozrenska Street only because she knew that that was the closest Serbian position? Did she have any other elements at her disposal to draw her conclusion from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know if the witness had any other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He believes that the confrontation line on Ozrenska Street was 700 metres away, and from your measurements we can see that it was over 1.000 metres away. Can you draw a conclusion, an unambiguous conclusion, that the bullet, indeed, originated from Ozrenska Street, or do you adhere to what you said, that it came from an area ranging from 200 metres to 1.104 metres, that that's the area from which the bullet could have originated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not measure Ozrenska Street to be 1.100 metres. It's -- as you can see where the arrow points on page 75, the 1104 metres is south of Ozrenska Street, so it's not the exact same distance. But I do -- I did conclude that the bullet could come from within that field of fire. So it could be from a shorter distance or it could be from a longer distance. So approximately from 200 metres to 1100 metres, that's where the shot must have originated from. But I also said that the shot would be more likely to have come from a longer range because they would have a more dominating position of the street, the shooter there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we agree that we should deduct perhaps 100 metres from 1104 metres, Ozrenska Street would still be about a thousand metres from the place of the incident; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you in Ozrenska Street, and would you agree that its northern slope commands a view of the place of the incident and its southern side is turned towards Lukavica and the center of the city? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that the houses on the north side of the street would have a better view of the place of incidents. But could you clarify what you mean with "southern side"? Just the southern side of the street?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I meant south of the street is a south-facing slope, and the word I mentioned was not interpreted to you. Ozrenska Street is a ridge, a watershed ridge, and do you remember that its northern side is directed towards the place of the incident and its southern side towards the city, and that Ozrenska Street is on top of the place where the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the houses on both sides of the street were approximately at the same level. So on the south side of the street, you would also -- there would be gaps between the houses on the north side which would offer some houses on the southern side insight at the incident site as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have an opportunity to see that in a topographic map. Could the Court please produce 65 ter 14045, page 77. Let's look at the photos contained in your report. Could you please look at the photo and tell us what it depicts? Is the place of the incident somewhere towards the top part of the photo? And if it is, could you please mark it for us.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place of the incident would be -- sorry -- would be somewhere around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was this photo taken from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have described above in the text, the photo was taken from Ozrenska Street, at street level, so standing on the sidewalk between houses, so with clear view. From the houses, I would have a better view, but I did not have access to the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What size zoom was used to take this photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the camera that I used, there's an 18- to 200-millimetre zoom, but it's a digital camera, so it would be 25 millimetres to 300 millimetres zoom, but I do not remember -- I do not remember exactly which zoom was used and how much times I magnified it on the computer. So it doesn't necessarily -- it's four times magnification or six times, I could not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden, from this place to the foot of the hill or where the hill starts ascending, doesn't it seem to you that the place of the incident should be towards the very top of the photo? Look closely. Isn't that the straight part of the street? From that place to the slope, is the distance really how you assumed it was, 200 metres? Wouldn't you say that the crossroads where the incident happened is towards the very north and the top of the photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm checking it now. Just a moment. Just a moment, please. No, the location that I've just marked would be the location of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please be provided with the map, and could you please tell us whether Ozrenska Street is on the watershed ridge between the southern and northern slope, at the trig points 676 and 650? We have all the markings. Could you please look at the map, and could you confirm what I just said? If necessary, we will also record all that. Could the usher please provide the witness with the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will propose to take a break now, and in the meantime the witness can take a brief look at the map, and we can proceed after the break. We'll break for 25 minutes, which means we will resume at five to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before we move to Ozrenska Street, can I just ask you, Mr. van der Weijden, where was this photo taken from? You said it was taken from Ozrenska Street; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before which house number in Ozrenska Street, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you have that anywhere in your notes, it would be of assistance for us, because our team will visit the very same spot. Do you have any GPS coordinates from -- of the position from which you took the photo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not have it above the photo in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the coordinate. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can see it from the monitor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please note the date and your signature, and then we can admit this page into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That part will be admitted as Exhibit D666. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, I'd like it to be known that if this is based on the US [Realtime transcript read in error "GPS"] map that Mr. Karadzic was looking at yesterday, I just want to note for the record that we have identified inaccuracies in that map, and we don't necessarily accept it as being an accurate representation of the -- of the purported territory that it depicts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The record should read "US" not "GPS map." The map is produced by the United States Department of Defence, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I now direct your attention, Mr. van der Weijden, as well as the attention of the OTP and the Trial Chamber, to this section of the map in which one can see Ozrenska Street. And would you agree that the contour lines and the isobars depict that Ozrenska Street is a stretch along the ridge between the north and the south slopes?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. It's located on a slope. The "600" that you see to the left, the letters are pointed downwards. That indicates in maps that there's a slope upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that these peaks, the elevation 670 and 655, are very close to Ozrenska Street, and that in the continuation, the slope moves to both sides, and that the street is spread along the very ridge of the hill? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not spread on the ridge. It's spread along the slope, especially the section that I've marked with two black dots on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you agree that -- or could you establish now what is the distance between Ozrenska Street and the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I calculated it, and it was 825 metres from the same location that I've marked with a black dot on the -- just below Ozrenska Street, the triangle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Do we see the dot you marked? Could you put your marked version on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I had them marked on this one, this is the first, these tiny dots, yes, but I will put them on here [marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While looking -- I would like you to mark on the photocopied version while looking at the originals.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a sketch drawn of the original, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You don't have a photocopied version. You can explain --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Could the witness please receive what we all have received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He has it. So number 1 depicts the place of incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And number 2 depicts what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depicts the distance of 825 metres, according to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this is Ozrenska Street. It stretches from Moravska [phoen] Street towards these trigonometric points 655 and 670; is that correct? Can you see where it says "Ozrenska"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that there is no Serbian position closer to Ozrenska -- closer to the place of the incident than the one situated in Ozrenska Street, that that's the closest position that there was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you then draw a conclusion, without -- beyond any reasonable doubt, that the shooting came from the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please put your initials on this map, and can we then have it admitted into evidence, please? And as a memento, we can give you a clean copy.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This photocopy, marked, will be admitted as Exhibit D667. Correct, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D667, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I now please draw your attention to Incident 6 from the F list. If I can remind you, it's an incident which occurred on the 6th of January, 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to the description of this incident, Sanija Dzevlan was shot and wounded in her buttocks while riding her bicycle across a bridge between Dobrinja 2 to Dobrinja 3 on the 6th of January, 1994, at 1630 hours, by a burst of fire. She was shot with one bullet in the lowest part of her back. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you give the page number of your report, Mr. van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be 47 of the paper copy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On what part of the bridge in Dobrinja was Sanija Dzevlan wounded, according to the information you received?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was wounded, according to the information that I received, on the northern side of the bridge, on the north-east side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what was the direction she was moving in?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was moving from, more or less, south to north. She had just crossed the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the fire was opened from which side?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, from the general direction of east-east-south -- east-south-east, to her right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the distance between the place from which it was shot to the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two locations that would be possible. One is at 355 metres and the other is at 820 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And why not a position that would be between 0 and 355 or between 355 and 820 metres? Why just these two possible distances?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because those are open fields. So if the shooter would be there, he would be exposed to any fire from any side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So both the victim and the shooter had to be out in the open; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The victim was crossing the bridge, and the bridge had some screens in place, and I believe the shooter was in a building, because to be out in the open, as a shooter, he would expose himself and risk his own life by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we recall the previous incident in Ivana Krndelja Street, your conclusion is that the shooter had to be out in the open. Why couldn't he have been out in the open here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he would be exposed to all sides and would severely risk his life by that. He could be fired upon by all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How far from these screens on the bridge did Sanija Dzevlan move at the moment when she was hit? How far was she from the screens? She was screened while she was on the bridge, because the bridge is screened, so she moved away from the screen. And how long did she cycle before she was hit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for a short distance.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see 65 ter 14045, page 49. It's Mr. van der Weijden's document, and on page 49 are the photographs which we deem to be important. The incident begins on page 47, but the photograph that we are interested in is on page 48. But in the document, itself, it's page 49, so in e-court it's page 49. The ERN page is 0629-5274.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I was looking at the ELMO. Could we please see the upper photograph, and zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden, do you know who was where along this possible line between 0 to 820 metres? Which forces were positioned where?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that the street that runs from, roughly, north to south -- south to north, which I will mark with a blue line [marks], that -- that this was the separation line with the Muslim forces to the west of the line and the Serbian forces on the right of the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please place number 1 next to the line that you were told was the separation line.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it is at about 400 metres from the place of the incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But would you agree that from the buildings which are 400 metres away, you cannot see the bridge because the view is obstructed by the buildings which are at a distance of about 355 metres and located on the Muslim-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That's the same conclusion I draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So if the shot came from the Serbian position, then it had to be the distance of 820 metres, and that's roughly the distance from the church; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I please ask you to mark the place where the church is located, though we can see the mark of 820 metres. So you don't have to mark that, but can you just write the date and your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D668.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that a burst of fire or were these single shots, one of which hit Sanija Dzevlan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the witness statement, it was written that the bullets started to fly, so I assumed that they were -- there was a burst of fire from a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that explain why she was hit immediately after she appeared from behind the screen?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But would you agree that in case these were single shots, the shooter would need a little bit of time in order to see her through the sight, whereas in case of a burst of fire, that would not have been the case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Galic case, this witness stated that the barricade was made from two to three centimetres thick and two and a half high -- two and a half metres high metal sheets. So we can also tender this statement. Could we please see 65 ter 22520, page 2. We have the statement in English, and I will read it out in Serbian: "The barricade which was in the area of the bridge only covered the bridge from end to end. There was open space at each end. The barricade was made of metal boards, about two or three centimetres thick and about two and a half metres high."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So she could have been hit only immediately after she left the space which is sheltered by the barricade. Can we please have this statement admitted? And would you agree with that, and have you had a chance to see this statement? Did you have access to it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have it admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, what was the speed at which a bicycle moved; that is to say, this victim?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would estimate it at 10 to 15 kilometres per hour, maybe faster because she was passing a dangerous stretch, stretch of road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have already said that, but just to establish everything. So immediately after appearing from behind the shelter, which wouldn't have allowed a bullet to pass through, she entered the line of fire, and she was shot immediately after the shelter. So would you conclude that no one was aiming at her, but, rather, that she just entered into the line of fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not conclude that from this. As was written in the witness statement, the barricade was on the bridge and there were no barricades just before and after the bridge. So she was -- she had been visible just before getting on the bridge, which would give the shooter time to -- already to aim at the location from which she would appear, or even fire so she would, indeed, ride into the line of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a possibility, but it's not something that you established; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not specifically establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is what I said also one possibility, that there was fire and that she rode into the line of the bullet, considering, of course, that if that was Serbian fire, that the distance was 820 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be a possibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that this person was turned in the direction of north-south, moving along this axis, and that the fire came into her flank, the side of her body?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you estimate the precision of automatic weapons at a distance of 820 metres?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen machine-gunners hit targets at 600 metres with a single shot, so 820 metres would not be an extreme difficult distance for a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was she hit from a machine-gun? What was the calibre of the bullet that hit her?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the wound sustained, I would estimate it to be a 7.62 or a 7.92 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in this incident, we also do not have the bullet or the calibre. That means that we have to speculate; isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that 7.9 millimetres -- that the Serbian Army did not have automatic weapons with this calibre?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've stated in the previous days, I personally saw Serbian troops with machine-guns in that calibre during my time with UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But we have no evidence that this was machine-gun fire, because a machine-gun creates much greater noise; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It creates the same noise as a regular gun with the same bullet, only more rounds after each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the climate conditions in Sarajevo at 1630 hours on a day in January? When does the night fall in Sarajevo on the 6th of January?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have -- I would have to research that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that it's rather dark at the time and that darkness falls immediately after 16 hours [as interpreted], is that something that you understand, that you will accept?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, darkness never falls immediately; there's always twilight. But not after -- 16 hours would be very early. But somewhere around that time, within a few hours, it would be dark, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that at 1630 in the Sarajevo Valley, the twilight is already quite thick, is that something that you would accept? We can check that. We can wait until the 6th of January and then see what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that the surroundings have an impact on the level of twilight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to the statement, the first sentence says: [In English] "On 6th of January, 1994, at around 1630 hours, I was returning home by my bicycle. At that moment, I was on the bridge in Nikola Demonja Street when bullets started to fly that were fired from Dobrinja 4, which is under the control of aggressor."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have that statement before us, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid not. It's 65 ter 22518. The previous one has been admitted. If not, could it please be admitted? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The previous one has been admitted. And what are you reading from now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading from a hard copy. Could the Court please produce 65 ter 22518. The previous statement described the barricade on the bridge, and this one actually depicts the events, what happened and when. It says here that bullets started flying and that they were fired from Dobrinja 4. She also says that Dobrinja 4 is under the control of the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there any dispute that the incident happened around 1630 hours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does Mr. van der Weijden agree that the incident happened at the time indicated by the witness, herself?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree to that if she states that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. By some sort of miracle, in the Galic judgement the time has moved between 1500 and 1600 hours in order to avoid the twilight. I'm afraid that this might appear as an adjudicated fact; therefore, I would like to correct that and establish facts correctly. When you drafted your report, you took into account the time indicated by this witness, by the victim?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your statement is a totally inappropriate statement. Can you answer the question, Mr. van der Weijden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took into account the time that it was daylight when the victim was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The transcript should have read your previous statement is an inappropriate statement. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have any elements that would point to a different time, a time different from the time indicated by the witness?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that you took into account what the witness wrote down, herself, in her own hand?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on your experience, would it be important, for a sharpshooter or a sniper, what time of day it is when they open fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a sharpshooter or a sniper, the time of day is always important. It also depends on what equipment was available. But I did not conclude anywhere it was a sharpshooter or a sniper.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this statement into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D670.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can I now remind you of Incident 9 from Schedule F, Mr. van der Weijden. Could you please consult your notes, and let's deal with that particular incident. If I'm not mistaken, you will find it on page 67 in your report. Right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the incident happened in a military field on the 26th of June, 1994, in the former Djure Jaksica Street and currently at the Adija Mulabegovica Street?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the exact name of the street, it was only given to me in the situation. The coordinate I had of the location was only pointed out to me by the investigator, and I took the GPS reading. And as for a military area, I only know that there were uniformed soldiers nearby, but I do not know that it was on a military field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The name of the locality or the neighbourhood is Vojnicko Polje, or the military field. The investigator of the OTP pointed out the place of the incidents to you, and his brief to you was to find the location from which the shot was fired; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As a result of the incident, a 16-year-old girl was shot and wounded in her right shoulder. According to the testimony of her girlfriend, after the wounding, BiH Army soldiers helped the girl, and allegedly they were not armed. The soldiers had been on the second or the third floor. The two girls accused the Serbs for the incident, and they said that the shots had been fired from the Institute for Blind Children. Right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall all the details, but the alleged shooting position was the School of the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was it who first mentioned the School for the Blind as the place where the sniper nest was and as the place where the shots came from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it in the initial documents provided to me by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the document where that could be found? And, secondly, where did the OTP find the School for the Blind to put it in that document, if it was, indeed, the OTP that had come up with that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was first mentioned by -- yeah, by the OTP, and that was the location of -- that was the place where they -- what the alleged shooting position was. I cannot remember at the moment where that document is. And where the OTP found the School of the Blind, I would not know, but it must have been stated, since this was used in a different trial as well, also from the UNMO and other witnesses, that it was a sniping nest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I then right when I say that you were expected to confirm what the OTP thought was correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My task was to go to the incident site and see what possibilities were there to take -- that would have a clear sight of the incident and would offer possibilities for shooters to have a location. So I did take into account the School of the Blind because that was within that area, but I did not solely take into account the School of the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That means that besides the School for Blind Children, you considered some other locations as well; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the Court please produce 65 ter 14045, which is Mr. van der Weijden's document. Page 70, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to be produced, let me ask you: Did you go to the place of this incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, because that was the location from where photo 2 was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where was this photo taken from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the actual incident site, as pointed to me by the investigator and taken from the GPS coordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. So the person taking the photo was standing at the place of the incident. What does the photo then depict?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we referring to photo 2? It says photo 1 is taken from --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd rather talk about photo 1. I would love to be able to do away with photo 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What does it depict?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photo 1 is a photo taken from the site of the School of the Blind, because the site had allegedly been used during the war, the windows that had been there at the time allegedly had been near bricked up. So I had to take a picture from the south-eastern side of the -- of that building. And it offers a view of the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Taken from the assumed place from which the shots were fired; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And, again, what is the zoom?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the same as before, taken with a digital camera with an 18- to 200-millimetre lens, which would translate, for a digital camera, to a 25, 26 to 300 millimetre. But I could not establish the magnification for this photo. Excuse me, that's 25 to 300 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have a photo in a normal scale, 1:1, the way a naked eye would see from the school to the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I estimate it about to be the same, because the school is only about 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between the place of the incident and the school, and we're still thinking of the school as one of the possible places, where was the separation line? Did they ever tell you where the separation line was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. I knew -- I was told that the School of the Blind was occupied by Serb troops, and there were Bosnian soldiers helping the girl, so they would be in the buildings next to the site of the incident. But I'm not aware of the exact separation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, you were told that the area had been taken by the Muslim Army and that the Muslim troops were also on the separation line in their own trenches; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you determine where the girl was at the moment when she was wounded; based on what? Was she on the ground or was she in a building, on the ground floor? Where was she?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was situated on the corner of the building. The terrace or the covered terrace that you see on the building now apparently wasn't there at the time of the incident, and she was standing at the corner of the building, or she was appearing at the corner of the building to which the blue arrow points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here, we have an obstacle on the opposite side, and we have again 180 degrees as a possibility of the range from which the bullet originated. Did you take into account any other possibility, any other location from which the bullet might have originated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My method is to go to a location, view the surroundings, see what technical and tactical possibilities there are, and eliminate the ones that are impossible or are very unlikely. So I did take into account all possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you take a photo of any of the possible places that were eventually eliminated by you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In photo 2, the building, the School of the Blind, is marked, but the whole area I took into account. But if I would move to the right with that picture, there would be no view of the victim. And the parking garage would be an impossible position for a shooter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you then sure? Have you established beyond any reasonable doubt that the shot was fired from the second floor of the School for the Blind or, for that matter, anywhere in the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, the shot was indeed fired from the School of the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could the bullet have originated from anywhere else? The range was 180 degrees. The whole side of the building could have been the shooting position, so do you think that the bullet could have originated from somewhere else, from another site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the range would actually be 270 degrees because she was standing on the corner, and that would eliminate about 90 degrees of the circle. The bullet -- the position that I started with was 270 degrees, and then I eliminated possibilities, ending up with the School of the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many degrees would have allowed for the possibility for a bullet to originate from there? Or let me put it differently. What was the range from which the bullet could have originated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I would look at the flat terrain, the bullet could have -- could have originated from up to a thousand metres, if there was -- if there were only flat terrain and no separation line, no buildings, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's if you assumed that the bullet must have originated from the Serbian side. But let's assume you don't know. What is the area, in degrees, that was open to bullet fire? Let's not talk about any separation lines or who could have fired the shots. How open to bullet fire was the victim's position? What was the range between the victim and the possible place from which the bullet was fired, in degrees?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In degrees, it would be 270 degrees, as I've stated before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any elements describing the position of the bullet canal in the body? Where did the bullet enter, where did it exit? Do you have any information about the position of the girl's body when the bullet entered the body, and how did the bullet travel, and where did it exit?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the Court please produce 1D02412.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to pay attention to the photo. Look at the arrow. Does it show in the direction of the School for the Blind? Further on, is there another arrow pointing to Dobrinja, on the one side, and Bulevar Mese Selimovica? And, finally, where it says the place of the incident, is this, indeed, the place where the incident happened, and is there an open line of vision towards the school and towards the street in front of it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not conclude anything from this picture. I recognise the high-rise building as being similar to the high-rise building in my pictures, but for the rest, I don't recognize any features.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that there are no major obstacles here, not only in front of the School for the Blind, but also in front of any other facilities? Do you agree that there are no obstacles and that shots could be fired from a closer or a more distant range? There are no obstacles anywhere, unless your brief was to determine that the shots had come from the Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I could not conclude anything from this picture, since I don't recognize the exact location.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce page 68 in Mr. van der Weijden's document, 014 -- 14045. We'll use your photo, and we will try to see how accurate we can be. Can the upper photo please be blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. van der Weijden, can you tell us, what does the photo depict?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photo depicts the incident site as well as the alleged shooting position, which I believe is the position which was fired from, with the angle of degrees from the shooting position towards the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now could you please pay attention to the entire 180 degrees that I insist on. Let us put the baseline or the tangent line on this street where the incident happened. Why do you think that shots could not have originated from any of the other degrees? Why did you eliminate all the other possibilities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this -- [marks]. In this area, the girl had already been visible for a long time because she had been coming from this direction [marks], so I don't think the shooter would have waited until she was getting to the corner and possibly disappearing into a trench. So this is why I left out this area [marks]. Down this street [marks], it would be difficult to see her because she was just appearing at the corner, which would give the shooter a very short reaction time to hit her standing at the corner. And within this region, this arc [marks], this is blocked by an almost blind bowl, and this is the parking area that blocks the view and which would offer a very limited -- no tactical position for a shooter. So this is why I came up to the School of the Blind, or the building known as the School of the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's a building marked with "190 metres"; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how high is the building across which the red line is drawn between the firing position and the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no building. From the top floor, the dark spot -- dark area, that's the shadow caused by the sun on the building to the south of it. That would be this dark area that's a shadow [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shadow of this building to the south of it [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if the shooter was at the School for the Blind, in the northern-most section, he had to take aim right against the corner of this building which casts the shadow in order to hit the target; correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not be very far from the corner, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And please tell us, was it established beyond doubt that the girl was hit by sniper, or could it have been any sort of single-shot fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been any sort of single shot. I do not know if it was a sniper, nor do I know his training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We don't know what calibre it was; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And we don't know in which direction the girl was turned, which direction she was facing; right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly; only that she was approaching -- she was on the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just ask you to draw a line marking the separation line on this photograph, because on the photograph below they showed you that. Can you please draw this line, the confrontation line, along this photograph. If it would help you, maybe we can lower what we can see on the screen a little bit so that you see the photo below, but it seems we cannot tamper with this photo until it is admitted. So can you please draw the separation lines or confrontation lines on this particular photo.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not. I only am aware that the School of the Blind was indicated as a Serb position and that there were soldiers nearby. There was a trench located between these buildings -- sorry, I'll mark this with green [marks]. But to my information, that trench was for people to cross the street, so I do not know if it's exactly at the separation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we keep this, could you put number 1 for those areas you excluded from the shooting area because the shooter must have a full view of the victim beforehand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir [marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And number 2 is along the road because the shooter could not have enough time to prepare.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay [marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And number 3 for the parking area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And number 4 for the shade of the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's enough. You marked the trench as green, so you don't have to put a separate number. Put the date and signature, please, Mr. van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be exhibited as Exhibit D ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D671, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 1D02413 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2413, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you seen traces on the facades of neighbouring buildings on both sides of the separation line, on the basis of which you might conclude that there was an exchange of fire taking place constantly in that area, and does this photograph show that to you? Would you agree that this the School for the Blind?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building appears to have a different roof structure than the building that I have taken a picture of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could this be the old-age pensioners' home? Have you taken note of this building which is right next to the separation line?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know any old-age pensioners' home, and I do not know where the separation line exactly was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. If this is the old-age pensioners' home situated at the front-line, does this photograph suggest that there was a constant exchange of fire, probably during a long period of time, because the facade of this building is full of various pockmarks that seem to testify to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us move on. This witness does not know whether this is situated in the front-line, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
